newsitem.title: FRANCE: Dexia sees '97 profit exceeding 3 bln Ffr.
newsitem.headline: Dexia sees '97 profit exceeding 3 bln Ffr.

text.p: Dexia, the banking group formed by the merger of Credit Local de France (CLF) and Credit Communal de Belgique, expects combined profit of more than three billion francs in 1997, its chairman said on Saturday.
The dividend paid out by the group should increase from the previous year, and Dexia intends to grow through acquisitions, Pierre Richard told French Radio Classique.
The group also aims to boost its return on shareholders' equity to 15 percent from a current 11 percent.
"The aim is to very quickly raise it to 13 percent and then to 15 percent," Richard said.
Acquisitions are also a priority. "We will develop by external growth in making major acquisitions from this year, and we will do it without any capital increase," he said.
"Our network must be completely European, and what we're lacking right now is Italy," he said.
He said former shareholders of CLF who are now Dexia shareholders should see a profit per share that "will be higher than the forecasts we had made initially, thanks to Dexia."

"Our aim is to have a dynamic group which will create shareholder value, and I would like...the group to have profits of around five billion francs by now and the year 2000," he said. ((-- Paris Newsroom +33 1 4221 5452))
